subject.title: Reject split outbound agent session ownership

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed for every explicit-agent and canonical-session owner mismatch, including recovery of already queued outbound entries, rather than retain explicit-agent precedence for existing contradictory callers?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes compatibility behavior across several public and internal outbound boundaries; source-level review can establish mechanics, but cannot choose the acceptable upgrade posture for existing integrations and queued work.

options.title: Adopt canonical-owner rejection
options.body: Confirm that explicit agent IDs, canonical control keys, and transcript mirror keys must always name the same normalized agent, then require exact-head proof before landing.

options.title: Preserve explicit-agent precedence
options.body: Keep the existing contradictory request shape working and narrow this PR to diagnostics or a separately opted-in strict mode if that remains the desired compatibility contract.

options.title: Defer the contract change
options.body: Pause this PR and retain the linked issue until an owner defines the supported cross-agent routing and queued-delivery migration policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt canonical-owner rejection
recommendation.body: Confirm that explicit agent IDs, canonical control keys, and transcript mirror keys must always name the same normalized agent, then require exact-head proof before landing.
